observation_summary: A unit test fails: multiplying a Dfp value by 10000 yields NaN with IEEE flag set (Multiply #37). The bug report states Dfp.multiply(int n) is limited to 0 <= n <= 9999, violating the FieldElement.multiply(int) contract.
reasoning_summary: The failure is caused by an implementation-level limitation in the multiply(int) procedure that incorrectly handles values outside 0..9999. This is a wrong computational/algorithmic behavior in the method (range-limited logic), not a missing guard, incorrect assignment, interface mismatch, timing issue, or high-level design omission. The fix is expected to change the method's algorithm to support arbitrary int operands.
evidence_used: failing_tests[0].headline: junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: assersion failed Multiply #37 x = NaN flags = 1
production_code_snippets: DfpTest lines 905-913 showing test(field.newDfp("1").multiply(10000), field.newDfp("10000"), 0, "Multiply #37")
bug_report_description: multiply(int n) is limited to 0 <= n <= 9999 and does not comply with FieldElement.multiply(int n) contract
evidence_gaps: No pre-fix source code for Dfp.multiply(int) method provided (exact implementation details of the limiting logic not shown).
No diff or proposed fix available to confirm the exact change type (though bug report implies algorithm change).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: Symptoms do not indicate a missing/incorrect guard or boundary check; the method is explicitly range-limited by algorithm rather than failing due to an absent validation.
The issue is not a single incorrect constant or variable initialization; tests show incorrect behavior for out-of-range inputs implying algorithmic limitation.
There is no indication of a contract/signature mismatch between components; the failure is internal to the multiply(int) implementation.
No concurrency, ordering, or serialization concerns are evident in the failure or description.
The defect does not appear to be due to inconsistent associations between data structures or procedures across components.
The capability (multiply by an integer) exists but is incorrectly implemented for some inputs; this is not a missing class/function or a design-level capability omission.
